records.arabic: بن سفيان الكلابية ذكرها أبو عمر فقال قال بن إسحاق تزوجها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد وفاة ابنته زنيب وخيرها حين أنزلت آية التخيير فاختارت الدنيا ففارقها فكانت بعد ذلك تلتقط البعر وتقول أنا الشقية اخترت الدنيا قال أبو عمر هذا عندنا غير صحيح لأن بن شهاب يروي عن أبي سلمة وعروة عن عائشة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين خير أزواجه بدأ بها فاختارت الله ورسوله قال وتتابع أزواج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلهن على ذلك وقال قتادة وعكرمة كان عنده حين أخبرهن تسع نسوة وهن اللاتي توفي عنهن وكذا قال جماعة إن التي كانت تقول أنا الشقية هي التي استعاذت واختلف في المستعيذة اختلافا كثيرا ولا يصح فيها شيء وقد قيل إن الضحاك بن سفيان عرض عليه ابنته فاطمة وقال أنها لم تصدع قط فقال لا حاجة لي بها وقد قيل إنه تزوجها سنة ثمان انتهى كلام بن عبد البر ويحتاج كلامه إلى شرح وعليه في بعضه مؤاخذات أما حديث بن شهاب بما ذكر فهو في الصحيح لكن آخره وأبي سائر وأما قول قتادة فأخرجه وأما قول عكرمة فأخرجه وأما قوله وهن اللاتي توفي عنهن ففيه نظر لأن آية التخيير كانت وتزوج بعد ذلك وأما الذي قال إن التي كانت تقول أنا الشقية هي المستعيذة فهو قول حكاه الواقدي عن بن مناح قال استعاذت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم وهذا لا يبطل قول بن إسحاق إن الكلابية اختارت وكانت تقول أنا الشقية لأن الجمع ممكن وأما قوله اختلف في المستعيذة اختلافا كثيرا فهو حق فقال بن سعد اختلف علينا في الكلابية اختلف علينا في اسمها فقيل فاطمة بنت الضحاك بن سفيان وقيل عمرة بنت يزيد بن عبيد وقيل سنا بنت سفيان بن عوف ثم قيل هي واحدة اختلف في اسمها وقيل ثلاث ثم أسند عن الواقدي عن بن أخي الزهري عن الزهري قال هي فاطمة بنت الضحاك دخل عليها فاستعاذت منه فطلقها فكانت تلقط البعر وتقول أنا الشقية وأسنده بالسند المذكور عن الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة قالت تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم الكلابية فلما دخلت عليه فدنا منها قالت أعوذ بالله منك فقال لقد عذت بعظيم الحقي بأهلك ومن طريق عبد الواحد بن أبي عون عن أم مناح بتشديد النون وبالمهملة قالت كانت التي استعاذت قد ولهت وذهب عقلها وكانت تقول إذا استأذنت على أمهات المؤمنين أنا الشقية وتقول إنما خدعت ومن طريق عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده كان دخل بها ولكنه لما خير نساءه اختارت قومها ففارقها فكانت تلقط البعر وتقول أنا الشقية وقيل إن المستعيذة سنا بنت النعمان بن أبي الجرن أسنده بن سعد عن الواقدي عن محمد بن يعقوب بن عتبة عن عبد الواحد بن أبي عون وقيل أسماء بنت النعمان بن أبي الجون أسنده عن الواقدي عن عمرو بن صالح عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبزي عن هشام بن الكلبي عن أبيه عن أبي صالح عن بن عباس ومن طريق أبي أسيد الساعدي كالقصة التي في الصحيح وفي آخرها فكانت تقول ادعوني الشقية ومن وجه آخر عن أبي أسيد أن المستعيذة توفيت في خلافة عثمان وأما قوله ولا يصح منها شيء فعجيب فقد ثبتت قصتها في الصحيح من حديث أبي أسيد الساعدي إلا أن كان مراده بنفي الصحة الجزم بالكلابية دون غيرها فهو ممكن على بعده وأما قوله إن الضحاك بن سفيان عرض عليه ابنته وقال أنها لم تصدع فأخرجه في الصحيح وأما قوله وقد قيل إنه تزوجها سنة ثمان فالظاهر أن الضمير لصاحبه الترجمة ومقتضاه أنه تقدم قول يخالفه ولم يتقدم إلا قوله في أول الترجمة إنه تزوجها بعد وفاة ابنته زينب وقد أسند بن سعد عن الواقدي عن إبراهيم بن وثيمة عن أبي وجزة قال تزوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الكلابية في ذي القعدة سنة ثمان منصرفه من الجعرانة وعن إسماعيل بن مصعب عن شيخ من رهطها أنها توفيت سنة ستين
records.english: Ibn Sufyān, the Kilābī woman. Abu ʿUmar mentioned her and said: Ibn Ishaq said that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم married her after the death of his daughter Zaynab. When the verse offering the choice was revealed, he gave her a choice; she chose this world, and he separated from her. Afterward she used to pick up dung pellets and say, “I am the wretched woman; I chose this world.” Abu ʿUmar said: In our view this is not sound, because Ibn Shihab related from Abu Salamah and ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, that when the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم offered his wives the choice, he began with her, and she chose God and His Messenger. He said: All the wives of the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم followed one another in doing the same. Qatadah and ʿIkrimah said that at the time he gave them the choice he had nine wives, namely those who remained his wives until he died. A group likewise said that the woman who used to say, “I am the wretched woman,” was the one who sought refuge from him. There is extensive disagreement about the identity of the woman who sought refuge, and nothing concerning her is sound. It is also said that al-Dahhak b. Sufyan offered him his daughter Fatimah, saying that she had never suffered a headache, but he replied, “I have no need of her.” It is also said that he married her in the year eight. Here ends Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's discussion. His words require explanation, and objections may be made to some of them. As for Ibn Shihab's report as he cited it, it is in the Sahih, though its ending is “and all the others refused.” As for Qatadah's statement, it was transmitted; and as for ʿIkrimah's, it too was transmitted. As for his statement that those were the wives he left at his death, this requires consideration, because the verse offering the choice came earlier, and he married afterward. As for the assertion that the woman who used to say, “I am the wretched woman,” was the one who sought refuge, it is an opinion al-Waqidi reported from Ibn Manah: “She sought refuge from the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم.” This does not invalidate Ibn Ishaq's statement that the Kilabiyyah chose and used to say, “I am the wretched woman,” because the two accounts can be reconciled. His statement that there was extensive disagreement over the woman who sought refuge is correct. Ibn Saʿd said: “There was disagreement among us concerning the Kilabiyyah; there was disagreement among us concerning her name.” She was said to be Fatimah bt. al-Dahhak b. Sufyan, ʿAmrah bt. Yazid b. ʿUbayd, or Sana bt. Sufyan b. ʿAwf. It was then said that she was one woman whose name was disputed, and it was also said that they were three women. He then gave a chain from al-Waqidi, from Ibn Akhi al-Zuhri, from al-Zuhri, who said: She was Fatimah bt. al-Dahhak. He entered upon her, and she sought refuge from him, so he divorced her. She then used to pick up dung pellets and say, “I am the wretched woman.” With the aforementioned chain, he also related from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, who said: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم married the Kilabiyyah. When he entered upon her and drew near, she said, “I seek refuge in God from you.” He replied, “You have sought refuge in One mighty; go back to your family.” Through ʿAbd al-Wahid b. Abi ʿAwn, from Umm Manah—with a doubled nun and the unpointed letter—she said: The woman who sought refuge became distraught and lost her reason. When she asked permission to enter upon the Mothers of the Believers, she used to say, “I am the wretched woman,” and would say, “I was only deceived.” Through ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather: He had consummated the marriage with her, but when he gave his wives the choice, she chose her own people, so he separated from her. She used to pick up dung pellets and say, “I am the wretched woman.” It is also said that the woman who sought refuge was Sana bt. al-Nuʿman b. Abi al-Jawn. Ibn Saʿd gave its chain from al-Waqidi, from Muhammad b. Yaʿqub b. ʿUtbah, from ʿAbd al-Wahid b. Abi ʿAwn. It is also said that she was Asmaʾ bt. al-Nuʿman b. Abi al-Jawn. He gave its chain from al-Waqidi, from ʿAmr b. Salih, from Saʿid b. ʿAbd al-Rahman b. Abza, from Hisham b. al-Kalbi, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas. Through Abu Usayd al-Saʿidi there is a version like the story in the Sahih; at its end, she used to say, “Call me the wretched woman.” Another route from Abu Usayd states that the woman who sought refuge died during ʿUthman's caliphate. As for Abu ʿUmar's statement that nothing about her is sound, it is surprising: her story is established in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Usayd al-Saʿidi. If, however, he meant that no categorical identification of her as the Kilabiyyah, rather than someone else, is sound, that interpretation is possible, though remote. As for his statement that al-Dahhak b. Sufyan offered him his daughter and said that she had never suffered a headache, it was transmitted in the Sahih. As for his statement, “It is said that he married her in the year eight,” the pronoun apparently refers to the subject of this biography. This implies that an earlier statement contradicted it, yet nothing preceded it except his opening statement that he married her after the death of his daughter Zaynab. Ibn Saʿd gave a chain from al-Waqidi, from Ibrahim b. Wathimah, from Abu Wajzah, who said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم married the Kilabiyyah in Dhu al-Qaʿdah of the year eight, on his return from al-Jiʿranah. And from Ismaʿil b. Musʿab, from an elder of her clan: She died in the year sixty.

Abi al-ʿAs, the paternal uncle of ʿUthman b. ʿAffan. She bore him ʿAʾishah, whom Marwan married and who bore him ʿAbd al-Malik. Al-Zubayr b. Bakkar mentioned this.

records.arabic: والدة عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي ذكرها أبو عمر فقال شهدت ولادة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين وضعته أمه آمنة وكان ذلك ليلا قالت فما شيء أنظر إليه من البيت إلا نور وإني لأنظر إلى النجوم تدنو حتى إني لأقول ليقعن علي قلت أسند ذلك أبو عمر
records.english: The mother of ʿUthmān ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ al-Thaqafī. Abu ʿUmar mentioned her and said: She witnessed the birth of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم when his mother Aminah delivered him. It was at night. She said, “Everything in the house upon which I looked was light, and I saw the stars draw so close that I thought they would fall upon me.” I say: Abu ʿUmar transmitted this with a chain.

records.arabic: بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس العبشمية أخت هند أم معاوية روت عنها أم محمد بن عجلان وهي مولاتها قاله أبو عمر قلت أسنده بن منده من طريق أبي بكر بن عياش عن محمد بن عجلان عن أمه عن فاطمة قالت قلت يا رسول الله ما كان على ظهر الأرض خباء أحب إلي أن يذلهم الله من أهل خبائك الحديث قال ورواه بن أبي أويس عن أبيه عن بن عجلان وزاد شيئا فيه والطبراني من طريق يعقوب بن محمد عن أبي بكر بن أويس عن أبي أيوب مولى القاسم عن بن عجلان عن أبيه عن فاطمة بنت عتبة أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة ذهب بها وبأختها فبايعتا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما اشترط قالت له هند هل تعلم في نساء قومك من هذه المنهيات شيئا فقال بايعيه فهكذا الشرط قال بن سعد تزوجها قرظة بن عبد عمرو بن نوفل بن عبد مناف فولدت له الوليد وهشاما ومسلما وعتبة وأبي بن قرظة وآمنه بنت قرظة وفاختة التي تزوجها معاوية ثم أسلمت وبايعت فتزوجها أبو حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة وأخرج بن سعد بسند صحيح عن بن أبي مليكة قال تزوج عقيل بن أبي طالب فاطمة بنت عتبة بن ربيعة فكانت تقول له إذا دخل أي عتبة بن ربيعة فقال لها يوما وقد أضجرته عن يسارك إذا دخلت النار فقالت لا يجمع رأسي ورأسك بيت وأتت عثمان فبعث معها بن عباس ومعاوية فوعداها فلما حضر وجداهما مصطلحين وأخرجه موصولا عن بن عباس باختصار وفي سنده الواقدي
records.english: Ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams, the ʿAbshamī woman. She was the sister of Hind, the mother of Muʿawiyah. Umm Muhammad b. ʿAjlan, her client, related from her. Abu ʿUmar said this. I say: Ibn Mandah gave its chain through Abu Bakr b. ʿAyyash, from Muhammad b. ʿAjlan, from his mother, from Fatimah, who said: I said, “O Messenger of God, there was no household on the face of the earth whose people I wished God to humiliate more than the people of your household,” to the end of the report. He said: Ibn Abi Uways related it from his father, from Ibn ʿAjlan, and added something to it. Al-Tabarani related, through Yaʿqub b. Muhammad, from Abu Bakr b. Uways, from Abu Ayyub, the client of al-Qasim, from Ibn ʿAjlan, from his father, from Fatimah bt. ʿUtbah: Abu Hudhayfah b. ʿUtbah took her and her sister, and the two gave the pledge to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. When he stipulated the conditions, Hind said to him, “Do you know any women among your people who commit any of these forbidden acts?” He replied, “Give him the pledge, for this is the condition.” Ibn Saʿd said: Qurazah b. ʿAbd ʿAmr b. Nawfal b. ʿAbd Manaf married her. She bore him al-Walid, Hisham, Muslim, ʿUtbah, Ubayy b. Qurazah, Aminah bt. Qurazah, and Fakhitah, whom Muʿawiyah married. Then she embraced Islam and gave the pledge, and Abu Hudhayfah b. ʿUtbah b. Rabiʿah married her. Ibn Saʿd transmitted with a sound chain from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: ʿAqil b. Abi Talib married Fatimah bt. ʿUtbah b. Rabiʿah. Whenever he entered, she would say to him, “Where is ʿUtbah b. Rabiʿah?” One day, after she had exasperated him, he replied, “To your left when you enter the Fire.” She said, “No house shall contain my head and yours.” She went to ʿUthman, who sent Ibn ʿAbbas and Muʿawiyah with her. They made promises to her; when the two arrived, they found the couple reconciled. Ibn Saʿd also transmitted it connected from Ibn ʿAbbas in an abridged form, though its chain contains al-Waqidi.

names.arabic: قرظة بن عبد عمرو بن نوفل بن عبد مناف
names.english: Qurazah b. ʿAbd ʿAmr b. Nawfal b. ʿAbd Manaf

names.arabic: فاطمة بنت عتبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس
names.english: Fāṭimah bint ʿUtbah Ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams

names.arabic: أبو حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة
names.english: Abu Hudhayfah b. ʿUtbah b. Rabiʿah

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد الله بن أبي قيس أم قهطم العامرية هاجرت مع زوجها سليط بن عمرو إلى الحبشة فولدت له سليط بن سليط كذا سماها وكناها بن سعد قال وأمها عاتكة بنت أسعد بن عامر بن بياضه الخزاعية وقال كانت قديما بمكة وبايعت وتقدم في ترجمة والدها أنها أم معظم فذلك كنيتها
records.english: Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays. She was Umm Qahtam al-ʿAmiriyyah. She emigrated with her husband Sulayt b. ʿAmr to Abyssinia and bore him Sulayt b. Sulayt. Thus Ibn Saʿd gave her name and kunya. He said: Her mother was ʿAtikah bt. Asʿad b. ʿAmir b. Bayadah al-Khuzaʿiyyah. He also said that she was in Mecca from early on and gave the pledge. It was stated previously in her father's biography that she was Umm Muʿazzam; that, then, was her kunya.

names.arabic: فاطمة بنت علقمة بن عبد الله بن أبي قيس
names.english: Fāṭimah bint ʿAlqamah Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays

names.arabic: عاتكة بنت أسعد بن عامر بن بياضه
names.english: ʿAtikah bt. Asʿad b. ʿAmir b. Bayadah

records.arabic: الأنصارية عمة جابر تقدم نسبها مع أخيها عمرو بن حرام ثبت ذكرها في الحديث الصحيح من رواية شعبة عن بن المنكدر عن جابر قال لما قتل أبي جعلت أكشف التراب عن وجهه والقوم ينهونني فجعلت عمتي فاطمة بنت عمرو تبكيه الحديث وهذا لفظ رواية الطيالسي عن شعبة
records.english: The Anṣārī woman. She was the paternal aunt of Jabir. Her lineage was given previously with her brother ʿAmr b. Haram. She is securely mentioned in the sound report related by Shuʿbah, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: “When my father was killed, I began uncovering the dust from his face while the people forbade me, and my paternal aunt Fatimah bt. ʿAmr began weeping for him,” to the end of the report. This is the wording of al-Tayalisi's transmission from Shuʿbah.

records.arabic: ذكرها أبو موسى في الذيل ونقل عن المستغفري أنه قال لها صحبة وجوز أبو موسى أنها التي قبلها
records.english: Abū Mūsā mentioned her in the Supplement. He transmitted from al-Mustaghfiri that he said she had companionship. Abu Musa allowed that she might be the preceding woman.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: القرشية الفهرية أخت الضحاك بن قيس تقدم نسبها في ترجمته وكانت أسن منه قال أبو عمر كانت من المهاجرات الأول وكانت ذات جمال وعقل وكانت عند أبي بكر بن حفص المخزومي فطلقها فتزوجت بعده أسامة بن زيد قلت وخبرها بذلك في الصحيح لما طلبت النفقة من وكيل زوجها فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتدى عند أم شريك ثم قال عند بن أم مكتوم فلما خطبت أشار عليها بأسامة بن زيد وهي قصة مشهورة وهي التي روت قصة الجساسة بطولها فانفردت بها مطولة رواها عنها الشعبي لما قدمت الكوفة على أخيها وهو أميرها وقد وقفت على بعضها من حديث جابر وغيره وقيل أنها أكبر من الضحاك بعشر سنين قاله أبو عمر قال وفي بيتها اجتمع أهل الشورى لما قتل عمر قال بن سعد أمها أميمة بنت ربيعة من بني كنانة
records.english: The Qurashī Fihrī woman. She was the sister of al-Dahhak b. Qays. Her lineage was given previously in his biography, and she was older than he. Abu ʿUmar said: She was one of the earliest female Emigrants, and was beautiful and intelligent. She was married to Abu Bakr b. Hafs al-Makhzumi, who divorced her; after him she married Usamah b. Zayd. I say: Her report concerning this is in the Sahih. When she requested maintenance from her husband's agent, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم told her, “Observe your waiting period in the house of Umm Sharik,” then said, “In the house of Ibn Umm Maktum.” When suitors sought her hand, he advised her to marry Usamah b. Zayd. It is a well-known story. She is also the sole narrator of the lengthy story of al-Jassasah in its full form. Al-Shaʿbi related it from her when she came to Kufa to join her brother, who was its governor. I have found parts of it in the hadith of Jabir and others. It is said that she was ten years older than al-Dahhak; Abu ʿUmar stated this. He said: The members of the consultative council assembled in her house after ʿUmar was killed. Ibn Saʿd said: Her mother was Umaymah bt. Rabiʿah of Banu Kinanah.

records.arabic: قيل هي بنت أبي حبيش وإن اسم أبي حبيش قيس
records.english: It is said that she was bint Abī Ḥubaysh. It is also said that Abu Hubaysh's name was Qays.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن عبد الله بن أبي قيس بن عبد ود بن نصر بن مالك بن حسل بن عامر بن لؤي القرشية العامرية تكنى أم جميل وهي بها أشهر قال بن إسحاق في رواية يونس بن بكير وغيره في مهاجرة الحبشة هاجر حاطب بن الحارث ومعه امرأته فاطمة بنت المجلل فتوفي زوجها هناك وقدمت المدينة هي وابناها مع أهل السفينتين فروى عبد الله بن الحارث بن محمد بن حاطب عن أبيه عن جده قال لما قدمنا من أرض الحبشة خرجت بن أمي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر الحديث المتقدم في محمد بن حاطب
records.english: Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays. Her lineage continues through ʿAbd Wudd b. Nasr b. Malik b. Hisl b. ʿAmir b. Luʾayy al-Qurashiyyah al-ʿAmiriyyah. Her kunya was Umm Jamil, by which she is better known. Ibn Ishaq said, in the recension of Yunus b. Bukayr and others, concerning the migration to Abyssinia: Hatib b. al-Harith emigrated accompanied by his wife Fatimah bt. al-Mujallal. Her husband died there, and she and her two sons came to Medina with the people of the two ships. ʿAbd Allah b. al-Harith b. Muhammad b. Hatib related from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “When we arrived from Abyssinia, my mother took me out to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم,” and he related the report given previously under Muhammad b. Hatib.

names.arabic: فاطمة بنت المجلل بن عبد الله بن أبي قيس
names.english: Fāṭimah bint al-Mujallal Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays

names.arabic: عبد الله بن الحارث بن محمد بن حاطب
names.english: ʿAbd Allah b. al-Harith b. Muhammad b. Hatib

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن خنساء بن مبذول الأنصارية من بني مازن بن النجار ذكرها بن حبيب في المبايعات وكذا ذكرها بن سعد وقال أنها أم ولد وتزوجها داود بن أبي داود بن عامر بن مالك بن خنساء فولدت له
records.english: Ibn ʿAmr ibn Khansāʾ ibn Mabdhūl, of the Anṣār and Banū Māzin ibn al-Najjār. Ibn Habib mentioned her among the women who gave the pledge, as did Ibn Saʿd. He said that she was the mother of a man's child. Dawud b. Abi Dawud b. ʿAmir b. Malik b. Khansaʾ married her, and she bore him children.

names.arabic: داود بن أبي داود بن عامر بن مالك بن خنساء
names.english: Dawud b. Abi Dawud b. ʿAmir b. Malik b. Khansaʾ

names.arabic: فاطمة بنت منقذ بن عمرو بن خنساء بن مبذول
names.english: Fāṭimah bint Munqidh Ibn ʿAmr ibn Khansāʾ ibn Mabdhūl

records.arabic: بن الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومية قتل أبوها باليمامة وأمها أم حكيم بنت أبي جهل وتزوج فاطمة المذكورة عثمان بن عفان فولدت له سعيدا والوليد ويقال إن اسمها أسماء
records.english: Ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, the Makhzūmī woman. Her father was killed at al-Yamamah, and her mother was Umm Hakim bt. Abi Jahl. ʿUthman b. ʿAffan married this Fatimah, and she bore him Saʿid and al-Walid. It is said that her name was Asmaʾ.

names.arabic: فاطمة بنت الوليد بن عبد شمس بن الوليد بن المغيرة
names.english: Fāṭimah bint al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Shams Ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah

title.arabic: فاطمة بنت الوليد بن عبد شمس
title.english: Fāṭimah bint al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Shams

records.arabic: بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس العبشمية قتل أبوها ببدر كافرا وتقدم ذكر عمتها فاطمة بنت عتبة وكانت هذه من المهاجرات الفاضلات زوجها عمها أبو حذيفة بن عقبة سالما الذي يقال له مولى أبو حذيفة فاستشهد باليمامة قال أبو عمر فخلف 34 عليها الحارث بن هشام كذا قال وفيه نظر بينه بن الأثير وصوب أن زوج الحارث بن هشام هي المكذورة بعد هذه وهو كما قال
records.english: Ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams, the ʿAbshamī woman. Her father was killed at Badr as an unbeliever. Her paternal aunt Fatimah bt. ʿUtbah was mentioned previously. This Fatimah was one of the virtuous female Emigrants. Her paternal uncle Abu Hudhayfah b. ʿUqbah married her to Salim, who was called the client of Abu Hudhayfah. Salim was martyred at al-Yamamah. Abu ʿUmar said: Al-Harith b. Hisham then married her [34]. So he said, but this requires examination. Ibn al-Athir explained it and correctly held that the wife of al-Harith b. Hisham was the woman mentioned immediately after this one. It is as he said.

names.arabic: فاطمة بنت الوليد بن عتبة بن ربيعة بن عبد شمس
names.english: Fāṭimah bint al-Walīd ibn ʿUtbah Ibn Rabīʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams

records.arabic: بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن مخزوم القرشية المخزومية أخت خالد بن الوليد قال بن سعد أمها حنتمة بمهملة مفتوحة ونون ساكنة ثم مثناة من فوق مفتوحة بنت عبد الله بن عمرو بن كعب الكنانية أسلمت يوم الفتح وبايعت وهي زوج الحارث بن هشام وهي والدة عبد الرحمن وأم حكيم ابني الحارث قال أبو عمر ويقال إن عمر تزوجها بعد الحارث وفيه نظر قلت وترجم لها بن منده فاطمة بنت الوليد القرشية وأورد لها حديث الإزار وقد أخرجه العقيلي من طريق عبد السلام بن حرب عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي فروة عن إبراهيم بن العباس بن الحارث عن أبي بكر بن الحارث عن فاطمة بنت الوليد أم أبي بكر أنها كانت بالشام تلبس الجباب من ثياب الخز ثم تأتزر فقيل لها ما يغنيك عن هذا الإزار فقالت سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم يأمر بالإزار قال بن الأثير قوله أم أبي بكر يعني بن عبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام فهي أم أبيه وهي جدة أبي بكر وهو كما قال فقد قال بن عساكر فاطمة بنت الوليد بن المغيرة أخت خالد لها صحبة وخرجت مع زوجها الحارث إلى الشام واستشارها خالد أخوها في بعض أمره روت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديثا واحدا رواه عنها بن ابنها أبو بكر بن عبد الرحمن فذكر حديث الإزار
records.english: Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Makhzūm, the Qurashī Makhzūmī woman. She was the sister of Khalid b. al-Walid. Ibn Saʿd said: Her mother was Hantamah—with an open unpointed ha, an unvocalized nun, then an open ta with two dots above—bt. ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr b. Kaʿb al-Kinaniyyah. She embraced Islam on the day of the Conquest and gave the pledge. She was the wife of al-Harith b. Hisham and the mother of his two children, ʿAbd al-Rahman and Umm Hakim. Abu ʿUmar said: It is said that ʿUmar married her after al-Harith; this requires examination. I say: Ibn Mandah gave her a biography as Fatimah bt. al-Walid al-Qurashiyyah and cited for her the report about the waist-wrapper. Al-ʿUqayli transmitted it through ʿAbd al-Salam b. Harb, from Ishaq b. ʿAbd Allah b. Abi Farwah, from Ibrahim b. al-ʿAbbas b. al-Harith, from Abu Bakr b. al-Harith, from Fatimah bt. al-Walid, mother of Abu Bakr: She was in Syria, wearing outer garments of silk brocade while also wrapping a waist-wrapper around herself. She was asked, “What benefit does this waist-wrapper give you?” She replied, “I heard the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم command the wearing of a waist-wrapper.” Ibn al-Athir said: The words “mother of Abu Bakr” mean the mother of ʿAbd al-Rahman b. al-Harith b. Hisham's father. She was therefore Abu Bakr's paternal grandmother. It is as he said. Ibn ʿAsakir said: Fatimah bt. al-Walid b. al-Mughirah, sister of Khalid, had companionship. She went to Syria with her husband al-Harith, and her brother Khalid consulted her about one of his affairs. She related one hadith from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Her grandson Abu Bakr b. ʿAbd al-Rahman related it from her. He then cited the report about the waist-wrapper.

records.english: It is said that this was the name of the client woman of Sālim, the client of Abī Ḥudhayfah.

records.arabic: العبسية أخت حذيفة تقدم نسبها في ترجمة حذيفة روت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها دخلت عليه تعوده في نسوة فإذا سقاء معلق يقطر ماؤه عليه من شدة ما يجد من حر الحمى وفيه إن أشد الناس بلاء الأنبياء ثم الذين يلونهم روى عنها بن أخيها أبو عبيدة بن حذيفة أخرج حديثها النسائي وابن سعد بسند قوي ورويناه بعلو في المعرفة لابن منده وفي جزء بن مسعود بن الفرات وقال بن سعد أسلمت وبايعت وقال منصور عن ربعي بن حراش قلت لمجاهد حدثني ربعي عن امرأة عن أخت حذيفة وكانت له أخوات أدركن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال مجاهد قد أدركتهن الحديث في دم التحلي بالذهب
records.english: The ʿAbsī woman. She was the sister of Hudhayfah. Her lineage was given previously in Hudhayfah's biography. She related from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم that she entered upon him with a group of women to visit him during his illness. A waterskin hung above him, its water dripping upon him because of the intense heat he suffered from the fever. The report includes: “The people most severely tried are the prophets, then those who come after them.” Her nephew Abu ʿUbaydah b. Hudhayfah related from her. Al-Nasaʾi and Ibn Saʿd transmitted her report with a strong chain. We related it through an elevated chain in Ibn Mandah's al-Maʿrifah and in the fascicle of Ibn Masʿud b. al-Furat. Ibn Saʿd said: She embraced Islam and gave the pledge. Mansur related from Ribʿi b. Hirash: I said to Mujahid, “Ribʿi related to me from a woman, from Hudhayfah's sister—and he had sisters who lived to meet the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.” Mujahid said, “I met them,” followed by the report condemning adornment with gold.

records.arabic: بفتح الفاء وسكون الراء وفتح المثناة الفوقانية بعدها نون إحدى القينتين اللتين كان بن خطل يعلمهما الغناء بهجاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم وأصحابه فكانتا ممن أهدر دمهما يوم الفتح فأسلمت هذه فتركت وقتلت الأخرى قاله السهيلي
records.english: With an open fāʾ, a quiescent rāʾ, and an open tāʾ above followed by nūn. She was one of the two singing girls whom Ibn Khatal taught songs satirizing the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم and his Companions. The blood of both was declared licit on the day of the Conquest. This woman embraced Islam and was spared, while the other was killed. Al-Suhayli stated this.

records.english: The ʿAtwārī woman. She was the mother of ʿUqaylah. She appeared previously under ʿUqaylah. I read it with fa and unvocalized ra in al-Khatib's handwriting.

names.english: Furayʿah bint Abī Umāmah Asʿad ibn Zurārah

records.english: Ibn Rāfiʿ ibn Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿUbayd ibn al-Jarrāḥ, of the Anṣār. She was of Banu al-Abjar. Ibn Habib mentioned her among the women who gave the pledge.

بن خنيس بن لودان الأنصارية والدة حسان بن ثابت وإليها كان ينسب فيقال قال بن الفريعة ونسب هو نفسه إليها في قوله

records.english: Ibn Khunays ibn Lawdhān, of the Anṣār. She was the mother of Hassan b. Thabit. He was attributed to her and was called Ibn al-Furayʿah. He himself traced his affiliation to her in his verse: “Those called al-Jalābīb have now become mighty and grown great, / while Ibn al-Furayʿah has become the town's ‘egg’ [an idiom of uncertain force].” Ibn Saʿd mentioned her among the women who gave the pledge. It is said that her father's name was ʿAmr.

records.arabic: الخدرية أخت أبي سعيد تقدم نسبها في ترجمة أخيها كذا عند الأكثر ووقع في سنن النسائي في سياق حديثها الفارعة وعند الطحاوي الفرعة وأمها حبيبة بنت عبد الله بن أبي ومدار حديثها على سعد بن إسحاق بن كعب بن عجرة عن عمته زينب بنت كعب بن عجرة أن الفريعة بنت مالك بن سنان وهي أخت أبي سعيد الخدري أخبرتها أنها جاءت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم تسأله أن ترجع إلى أهلها في بني خدرة فإن زوجها خرج في طلب أعبد له أبقوا فقتل فذكر الحديث وفيه امكثي في بيتك حتى يبلغ الكتاب أجله وفيه فلما كان عثمان بن عفان أرسل إلي يسألني فأخبرته فاتبعه وقضى به رواه مالك في الموطأ عن سعد بن إسحاق ورواه الناس بن مالك عن شيخه الزهري قال بن منده أخبرنا محمد بن محمد بن يعقوب النيسابوري حدثنا محمد بن سليمان بن الحارث حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله النساج حدثنا أحمد بن سيف بن سعيد حدثني أبي عن يونس بن يزيد عن بن شهاب حدثني من يقال له مالك بن أنس فذكره
records.english: The Khudrī woman. She was the sister of Abu Saʿid. Her lineage was given previously in her brother's biography. This is the form used by most authorities. In the wording of her report in the Sunan of al-Nasaʾi, however, it appears as al-Fariʿah, and in al-Tahawi as al-Farʿah. Her mother was Habibah bt. ʿAbd Allah b. Ubayy. Her report turns on Saʿd b. Ishaq b. Kaʿb b. ʿUjrah, from his paternal aunt Zaynab bt. Kaʿb b. ʿUjrah: Furayʿah bt. Malik b. Sinan, sister of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, informed her that she came to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله وسلم to ask whether she could return to her family among Banu Khudrah, because her husband had gone in pursuit of slaves of his who had absconded, and they killed him. He then related the report, which includes: “Remain in your house until the prescribed term reaches its end.” It also says: “When ʿUthman b. ʿAffan became caliph, he sent for me to ask me, and I informed him; he followed it and judged accordingly.” Malik related it in al-Muwattaʾ from Saʿd b. Ishaq. The people related it from Malik, from his shaykh al-Zuhri. Ibn Mandah said: Muhammad b. Muhammad b. Yaʿqub al-Naysaburi informed us; Muhammad b. Sulayman b. al-Harith related to us; Ahmad b. ʿAbd Allah al-Nassaj related to us; Ahmad b. Sayf b. Saʿid related to us; my father related to me, from Yunus b. Yazid, from Ibn Shihab: one who was called Malik b. Anas related to me—and he cited it.

records.arabic: بن عفراء الأنصارية أخت الربيع تقدم نسبها في أبيها قال أبو عمر لها صحبة حديثها في الرخصة في الغناء وضرب الدف في العرس من حديث أهل البصرة وقال بن منده روى حديثها خالد بن دينار عن أمه عنها أنها دخلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
records.english: Ibn ʿAfrāʾ, of the Anṣār. She was the sister of al-Rubayyiʿ. Her lineage was given previously under her father. Abu ʿUmar said: She had companionship. Her report, among the reports of the people of Basra, concerns the permission to sing and strike the tambourine at weddings. Ibn Mandah said: Khalid b. Dinar related her report from his mother, from Furayʿah, that she entered upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم.

records.arabic: الزهرية رفعها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده وقال من أراد أن ينظر إلي خالة رسول الله فلينظر إلى هذه ذكره أبو موسى في الذيل عن المستغفري وقال لم يزد على هذا قلت وقد تقدم شيء من هذا في فاختة بنت عمرو
records.english: The Zuhrī woman. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم lifted her with his hand and said, “Whoever wishes to look upon the maternal aunt of the Messenger of God, let him look at this woman.” Abu Musa mentioned it in the Supplement, from al-Mustaghfiri, and said that he added nothing further. I say: Something of this was given previously under Fakhitah bt. ʿAmr.

records.arabic: بفاء ومهملة مضمومتين بينهما سين مهملة ساكنة بنت أوس بن خولي بن عبد الله بن الحارث الأنصارية تقدم ذكر نسبها في والدها قال بن حبيب بايعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهي من بني الحبلي
records.english: With a fāʾ and an undotted ḥāʾ, both vowelled with ḍammah, and between them a quiescent undotted sīn. She was the daughter of Aws b. Khawli b. ʿAbd Allah b. al-Harith al-Ansariyyah. Her lineage was mentioned previously under her father. Ibn Habib said: She gave the pledge to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and was of Banu al-Hubla.

names.arabic: أوس بن خولي بن عبد الله بن الحارث
names.english: Aws b. Khawli b. ʿAbd Allah b. al-Harith

records.arabic: جارية فاطمة الزهراء أخرج أبو موسى في الذيل والثعلبي في تفسير سورة هل أتى من طريق عبد الله بن عبد الوهاب الخوارزمي بن عم الأحنف عن أحمد بن حماد المروزي عن محبوب بن حميد وسأله روح بن عبادة عن القاسم بن بهرام عن ليث بن أبي سليم عن مجاهد عن بن عباس في قوله تعالى يوفون بالنذر الآية قال مرض الحسن والحسين فعادهما جدهما صلى الله عليه وسلم وعادهما عامة العرب فقالوا لأبيهما لو نذرت فقال علي إن عوفيا صيام 341 ثلاثة أيام شكرا وقالت فاطمة كذلك وقالت جارية يقال لها فضة النوبية فذكر حديثا طويلا قال الذهبي كأنه موضوع وليس ما قاله ببعيد وذكر بن صخر في فوائده وابن بشكوال في كتاب المستغيثين من طريقه بسند له من طريق الحسين بن العلاء عن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي عن أبيه عن علي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخدم فاطمة ابنته جارية اسمها فضة النوبية وكانت تشاطرها الخدمة فعلمها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعاء تدعو به فقالت لها فاطمة أتعجنين أو تخبزين فقالت بل أعجن يا سيدتي وأحتطب فذهبت واحتطبت وبيدها حزمة وأرادت حملها فعجزت فدعت بالدعاء الذي علمها وهو يا واحد ليس كمثله أحد تميت كل أحد وتفنى كل أحد وأنت على عرشك واحد ولا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم فجاء أعرابي كأنه من أزد شنوءة فحمل الحزمة إلى باب فاطمة
records.english: A servant woman of Fāṭimah al-Zahrāʾ. Abu Musa transmitted in the Supplement, and al-Thaʿlabi in his commentary on Surat Hal Ata, through ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Khwarizmi, the cousin of al-Ahnaf, from Ahmad b. Hammad al-Marwazi, from Mahbub b. Humayd, who asked Rawh b. ʿUbadah about al-Qasim b. Bahram, from Layth b. Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying تعالى, “They fulfill their vows,” to the end of the verse. He said: Al-Hasan and al-Husayn fell ill, so their grandfather صلى الله عليه وسلم visited them, as did the generality of the Arabs. They said to their father, “If only you would make a vow.” ʿAli said, “If they recover, I shall fast [341] three days in gratitude.” Fatimah said the same, and a servant called Fiddah the Nubian likewise said it. He then related a lengthy report. Al-Dhahabi said: It appears fabricated. What he said is not far-fetched. Ibn Sakhr mentioned in his Fawaʾid, and Ibn Bashkuwal in the Book of Those Who Sought Aid, through Ibn Sakhr's route and with a chain of his through al-Husayn b. al-ʿAlaʾ, from Jaʿfar b. Muhammad b. ʿAli b. al-Husayn b. ʿAli, from his father, from ʿAli: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم assigned his daughter Fatimah a servant girl named Fiddah the Nubian. She and Fatimah divided the service equally. The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم taught her a supplication with which to pray. Fatimah asked her, “Will you knead, or bake?” She replied, “Rather, I shall knead, my lady, and gather firewood.” She went out, gathered wood, and held a bundle in her hand. She tried to carry it but could not, so she recited the supplication he had taught her: “O One, unlike whom there is no one; You cause every person to die and bring every person to an end; You are One upon Your throne, and neither slumber nor sleep overtakes You.” A Bedouin, who appeared to be from Azd Shanuʾah, came and carried the bundle to Fatimah's door.

records.arabic: امرأة حصاب بن الحارث الجمحي ذكرها بن إسحاق فيمن أسلم قديما من المهاجرات وأخرج ذلك محمد بن عثمان بن أبي شيبة في تاريخه وأبو نعيم من طريقه من رواية زياد البكائي عن بن إسحاق وقال بن سعد أسلمت قديما بمكة وبايعت وهاجرت الهجرتين
records.english: The wife of Ḥaṣṣāb ibn al-Ḥārith al-Jumaḥī. Ibn Ishaq mentioned her among the female Emigrants who embraced Islam early. Muhammad b. ʿUthman b. Abi Shaybah transmitted this in his History, as did Abu Nuʿaym through his route, in the recension of Ziyad al-Bakkaʾi from Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Saʿd said: She embraced Islam early in Mecca, gave the pledge, and made both emigrations.

records.english: Ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar ibn Makhzūm. Her father died a martyr at al-Yamamah, and her mother was Umm Hakim bt. Abi Jahl. ʿUthman b. ʿAffan married her, and she bore him Saʿid and al-Walid. Al-Zubayr b. Bakkar mentioned her.

title.english: Fāṭimah bint al-Walīd ibn ʿAbd Shams

records.arabic: ظئر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أويت إلى فراشك فاقرئي قل يأيها الكافرون فإنها براءة من الشرك ذكرها أبو أحمد العسكري هكذا استدركها بن الأثير وأقره الذهبي وهو خطأ نشأ عن تحريف وإنما هو قال بغير تاء تأنيث فإن هذا معروف لفروة بن نوفل وهو رجل من التابعين غلط بعض الرواة عن بن إسحاق فقال عن فروة بن نوفل أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت والصواب ما رواه غيره فقال عن أبي إسحاق عن فروة بن نوفل الديلمي عن أبيه فذكره وقد بينته في القسم الرابع من حرف الفاء
records.english: The wet nurse of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. She said: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم told me, “When you retire to your bed, recite, ‘Say: O unbelievers,’ for it is a declaration of freedom from idolatry.” Abu Ahmad al-ʿAskari mentioned her thus. Ibn al-Athir included her as an addendum, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. This is an error that arose from a corruption: the source actually reads “he said,” without the feminine ta. This report is well known from Farwah b. Nawfal, a man of the Successors. Some transmitters erred in relating it from Ibn Ishaq, saying, “From Farwah b. Nawfal: I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and said...” The correct version is what others related: “from Abu Ishaq, from Farwah b. Nawfal al-Daylami, from his father,” and then he cited it. I explained this in Section Four of the letter fa.

records.arabic: أم إبراهيم بن نبيط لها صحبة ذكرها بن الأمين في ذيله على الاستيعاب كذا في التجريد واستدراكها وهم فإن أبا عمر ذكر في الفارعة بنت أبي أمامة أسعد بن زرارة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم زوجها نبيط بن جابر وقد ذكرت في الفارعة رواية من سماها الفريعة والإيراد في هذا على الذهبي أشد منه على بن الأمين وبالله التوفيق
records.english: The mother of Ibrāhīm ibn Nubayṭ. She had companionship. Ibn al-Amin mentioned her in his supplement to al-Istiʿab—thus in al-Tajrid. Including her as an addendum is an error, for Abu ʿUmar mentioned, under al-Fariʿah bt. Abi Umamah Asʿad b. Zurarah, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم married her to Nabit b. Jabir. Under al-Fariʿah I have cited a narration of one who named her al-Furayʿah. The criticism in this matter applies more strongly to al-Dhahabi than to Ibn al-Amin. وبالله التوفيق.

names.arabic: الفارعة بنت أبي أمامة أسعد بن زرارة
names.english: al-Fariʿah bt. Abi Umamah Asʿad b. Zurarah
Furayʿah The mother of Ibrāhīm ibn Nubayṭ

records.arabic: بن صخر بن خنساء زوج بشر بن البراء بن معرور ذكرها هكذا في التجريد وقد تقدم في الزاي زينب صيفي ولعلها أختها
records.english: Ibn Ṣakhr ibn Khansāʾ. She was the wife of Bishr b. al-Baraʾ b. Maʿrur. She was mentioned thus in al-Tajrid. Zaynab Sayfi was given previously under the letter zay; perhaps Qubaysah was her sister.

names.arabic: قبيسة بنت صيفي بن صخر بن خنساء
names.english: Qubaysah bint Ṣayfī Ibn Ṣakhr ibn Khansāʾ

records.arabic: بفتح أوله وسكون المثناة الفوقانية وقيل بالتصغير بنت عبد العزي بن سعد بن نصر بن مالك بن حسل بن عامر بن لؤي القرشية العامرية والدة أسماء بنت أبي بكر وشقيقها عبد الله كذا نسبها الزبير وغيره وقال أبو موسى في الذيل قتيلة بنت سعد بن عامر بن لؤي كذا اختصر النسب وحذف منه جماعة ثم قال أوردها المستغفري في الصحابيات وقال تأجر إسلامها وسماها الحاكم أبو أحمد في الكنى وحديثها عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق قالت قدمت على أمي وهي مشركة في عهد قريش ومدتهم فاستأذنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أصلها الحديث وهو في الصحيح وفي بعض طرقه وهي راغبة قال أبو موسى ليس في شيء من الروايات ذكر إسلامها وقولها راغبة ليست تريد في الإسلام بل في الصلة ولو كانت مسلمة لما احتاجت أسماء أن تستأذن في صلتها إلا أن تكون أسلمت بعد ذلك قلت إن كانت عاشت إلى الفتح فالظاهر أنها أسلمت
records.english: With its first letter open and the tāʾ above quiescent; it is also said in the diminutive. She was the daughter of ʿAbd al-ʿUzza b. Saʿd b. Nasr b. Malik b. Hisl b. ʿAmir b. Luʾayy al-Qurashiyyah al-ʿAmiriyyah. She was the mother of Asmaʾ bt. Abi Bakr and her full brother ʿAbd Allah. Thus al-Zubayr and others gave her lineage. Abu Musa said in the Supplement: “Qutaylah bt. Saʿd b. ʿAmir b. Luʾayy,” abbreviating the lineage and omitting several men. He then said: Al-Mustaghfiri included her among the female Companions and said that her conversion to Islam was late. Al-Hakim Abu Ahmad named her in the section on kunyas. Her report is from Hisham b. ʿUrwah, from his father, from Asmaʾ bt. Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: “My mother came to me while she was an idolater, during the period of Quraysh and their treaty. I asked the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم for permission to maintain relations with her,” to the end of the report. It is in the Sahih. In some routes it says, “while she was desirous.” Abu Musa said: None of the narrations mention her conversion to Islam. Her being “desirous” does not mean desirous of Islam, but desirous of maintaining relations. Had she been Muslim, Asmaʾ would not have needed to seek permission to maintain relations with her—unless she embraced Islam later. I say: If she lived until the Conquest, the apparent conclusion is that she embraced Islam.

names.arabic: عبد العزي بن سعد بن نصر بن مالك بن حسل بن عامر بن لؤي
names.english: ʿAbd al-ʿUzza b. Saʿd b. Nasr b. Malik b. Hisl b. ʿAmir b. Luʾayy

names.arabic: قتيلة بنت سعد بن عامر بن لؤي
names.english: Qutaylah bt. Saʿd b. ʿAmir b. Luʾayy

records.arabic: ويقال الأنصارية قال أبو عمر كانت من المهاجرات الأول روى عنها عبد الله بن يسار ولم أر من نسبها أنصارية وقوله من المهاجرات يأبى ذلك وقد أخرج حديثها بن سعد وأشار إلى أنها ليس لها غيره والطبراني من طريق مسعر عن سعيد بن خالد الجدلي عن عبد الله بن يسار عن قتيلة امرأة من جهينة قالت جاء يهودي وفي رواية بن سعد حبر من الأحبار إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إنكم تشركون تقولون ما شاء الله وشئت وتقولون والكعبة فأمرهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقولوا ما شاء الله ثم شئت وأخرجه النسائي وسنده صحيح وأخرجه بن منده من طريق المسعودي عن سعيد عن بن يسار عن قتيلة بنت صيفي الجهينة
records.english: She is also said to have been of the Anṣār. Abu ʿUmar said: She was one of the early female Emigrants. ʿAbd Allah b. Yasar related from her. I have not seen anyone give her lineage as an Ansari woman, and the statement that she was among the Emigrants precludes it. Ibn Saʿd transmitted her report and indicated that she had no other report. Al-Tabarani transmitted through Misʿar, from Saʿid b. Khalid al-Jadali, from ʿAbd Allah b. Yasar, from Qutaylah, a woman of Juhaynah, who said: A Jew came—or, in Ibn Saʿd's recension, a rabbi among the rabbis—to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and said, “You associate partners: you say, ‘What God wills and what you will,’ and you say, ‘By the Kaʿbah.’” The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم instructed them to say, “What God wills, then what you will.” Al-Nasaʾi transmitted it, and its chain is sound. Ibn Mandah transmitted it through al-Masʿudi, from Saʿid, from Ibn Yasar, from Qutaylah bt. Sayfi al-Juhaniyyah.

records.english: Of Banū Mālik ibn Ḥisl. She is mentioned. Ibn Mandah included her in abridged form, and Abu Nuʿaym followed him.

records.english: Ibn Hilāl, the Kinānī woman. She gave the pledge to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Ibn Habib and Ibn Saʿd stated this.

records.arabic:
بن الحارث بن علقمة بن كلدة بن عبد مناف بن عبد الدار بن قصي القرشية كانت زوج عبد الله بن الحارث بن أمية الأصغر فهي أم علي بن عبد الله وإخوته الوليد ومحمد وأم الحكم قال أبو عمر قال الواقدي هي التي قالت الأبيات القافية في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قتل أباها النضر بن الحارث يوم بدر
يا راكبا إن الأثيل مظنة
من صبح خامسة وأنت موفق
أبلغ به ميتا فإن تحية
ما إن تزال بها النجائب تخفق
مني إليه وعبرة مسفوحة
جادت لمائحها وأخرى تخنق
هل يسمعن النضر إن نادبته
بل كيف يسمع ميت لا ينطق
ظلت سيوف بني أبيه تنوشه
لله أرحام هناك تشقق
قسرا يقاد إلى المنية متعبا
رسف المقيد وهو عان موثق
أمحمد ولدتك خير نجيبة
في قومها والفحل فحل معرق
ما كان ضرك لو مننت وربما
من الفتى وهو المغيظ المحنق
فالنضر أقرب إن تركت قرابة
وأحقهم إن كان عتق يعتق فلما بلغ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك بكى حتى اخضلت لحيته وقال لو بلغني شعرها قبل أن أقتله ما قتلته قال أبو عمر هذا لفظ عبد الله بن إدريس وفي رواية الزبير بن بكار فرق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى دمعت عيناه وقال لأبي بكر يا أبا بكر لو سمنت شعرها لم أقتل أباها وقال الزبير سمعت بعض أهل العلم يغمز هذه الأبيات ويقول أنها مصنوعة قلت ولم أر التصريح بإسلامها لكن إن كانت عاشت إلى الفتح فهي من جملة الصحابيات ورأيت في آخر كتاب البيان للجاحظ أن اسمها ليلى وذكر أنها جذبت رداء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يطوف وأنشدته الأبيات المذكورة
records.english: Ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAlqamah ibn Kaladah ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn ʿAbd al-Dār ibn Quṣayy, the Qurashī woman. She was the wife of ʿAbd Allah b. al-Harith b. Umayyah the Younger, and was the mother of ʿAli b. ʿAbd Allah and his siblings al-Walid, Muhammad, and Umm al-Hakam. Abu ʿUmar said: Al-Waqidi said that she was the woman who addressed rhyming verses to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم after he killed her father al-Nadr b. al-Harith on the day of Badr: “O rider, al-Athil is the likely place, / at dawn on the fifth day, and you are granted success. / Convey to the dead man there a greeting, / for the noble mounts still race with it: / from me to him, and a tear poured forth, / one eye yielding to the one who draws it, the other choking back. / Can al-Nadr hear if I lament him? / But how can one who is dead and speaks not hear? / The swords of his father's sons continued reaching for him— / for God's sake, what bonds of kinship were torn there! / Compelled, weary, he was led to death, / shuffling like a fettered prisoner, captive and bound. / O Muhammad, the best of noblewomen bore you / among her people, and your sire was a deeply rooted stallion. / What harm would there have been had you granted favor? Often / favor comes from a young man though enraged and wrathful. / Al-Nadr was the closest in kinship, had you spared him, / and the most deserving of them, if any captive were to be freed.” When the verses reached the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم, he wept until his beard became wet and said, “Had her poetry reached me before I killed him, I would not have killed him.” Abu ʿUmar said: This is the wording of ʿAbd Allah b. Idris. In the narration of al-Zubayr b. Bakkar, the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم was moved to tenderness until his eyes filled with tears, and he said to Abu Bakr, “O Abu Bakr, had I heard her poetry, I would not have killed her father.” Al-Zubayr said: I heard some scholars impugn these verses and say that they were fabricated. I say: I have not seen an explicit statement that she embraced Islam. But if she lived until the Conquest, she belongs among the female Companions. At the end of al-Jahiz's Book of Eloquence, I saw that her name was Layla. He related that she pulled the mantle of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم while he was circumambulating and recited the aforementioned verses to him.

records.arabic: بفتح أوله ويقال بالتصغير بنت أبي أمية بن المغيرة المخزومية أخت أم سلمة تقدم نسبها في ترجمة أخيها عبد الله قالت أم سلمة لما وضعت زينب جاءني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فخطبني فذكرت قصة تزويجها ودخوله عليها واشتغالها برضاع زينب حتى جاء يوما فلم يرها فقال أين زينب فقالت قريبة ووافقها عبدها أخذها عمار بن ياسر فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنا آتيكم الليلة فدخل على أم سلمة وقال البلاذري تزوجها معاوية بن أبي سفيان لما أسلم وقال بن سعد هي قريبة الصغرى أمها عاتكة بنت عتبة بن ربيعة قال وتزوجها عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر فولدت له عبد الله وأم حكيم وحفصة ثم ساق بسند صحيح إلى بن أبي مليكة قال تزوج عبد الرحمن قريبة أخت أم سلمة وكان في خلفه شدة فقالت له يوما أما والله لقد حذرتك قال فأمرك بيدك قالت لا أختار على بن الصديق أحدا فأقام عليها قلت وكانت موصوفة بالجمال فقد وقع عند عمر بن شبة في كتاب مكة عن يعقوب بن القاسم الطلحي عن يحيى بن عبد الله بن أبي الحارث الزمعي قال لما فتحت مكة قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لسعد بن عبادة لما قال ما رأينا من نساء قريش ما كان يذكر من جمالهن هل رأيت بنات أبي أمية بن المغيرة هل رأيت قريبة الحديث
records.english: With its first letter open; it is also said in the diminutive. She was the daughter of Abi Umayyah b. al-Mughirah al-Makhzumiyyah, sister of Umm Salamah. Her lineage was given previously in the biography of her brother ʿAbd Allah. Umm Salamah said: When I gave birth to Zaynab, the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم came to me and proposed marriage. She related the story of her marriage, his entering upon her, and her being occupied nursing Zaynab, until one day he came and did not see the child. He asked, “Where is Zaynab?” Quraybah said, and her male servant agreed with her, “ʿAmmar b. Yasir took her.” The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “I shall come to you tonight,” and entered upon Umm Salamah. Al-Baladhuri said: Muʿawiyah b. Abi Sufyan married Quraybah when he embraced Islam. Ibn Saʿd said: She was Quraybah the Younger; her mother was ʿAtikah bt. ʿUtbah b. Rabiʿah. He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman b. Abi Bakr married her, and she bore him ʿAbd Allah, Umm Hakim, and Hafsah. He then gave a sound chain to Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman married Quraybah, sister of Umm Salamah, and there was harshness in his disposition. She said to him one day, “By God, I was warned about you.” He replied, “Your affair is in your own hands.” She said, “I would not choose anyone over the son of al-Siddiq,” and she remained with him. I say: She was known for beauty. In ʿUmar b. Shabbah's Book of Mecca, through Yaʿqub b. al-Qasim al-Talhi, from Yahya b. ʿAbd Allah b. Abi al-Harith al-Zamʿi: When Mecca was conquered, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said to Saʿd b. ʿUbadah, after Saʿd had said, “We have not seen among the women of Quraysh the beauty that used to be spoken of”: “Have you seen the daughters of Abu Umayyah b. al-Mughirah? Have you seen Quraybah?”—to the end of the report.

names.english: Yahya b. ʿAbd Allah b. Abi al-Harith al-Zamʿi

names.arabic: قريبة بنت زيد بن عبد ربه
names.english: Quraybah bint Zayd Ibn ʿAbd Rabbih

records.arabic: بن حرب الأموية أخت معاوية ذكرها صاحب التاريخ المظفري قال خطبها أربعة عشر رجلا من أهل بدر فأبت وتزوجت عقيل بن أبي طالب وقالت كان مع الأحبة يوم بدر تعني أباه وأخاه حنظلة وجدها عتبة وأخاه شيبة ومن كان معه من المشركين يوم بدر
records.english: Ibn Ḥarb, the Umayyad woman. She was the sister of Muʿawiyah. The author of al-Taʾrikh al-Muzaffari mentioned her. He said: Fourteen men who had fought at Badr proposed marriage to her, but she refused and married ʿAqil b. Abi Talib. She spoke of being “with the loved ones on the day of Badr,” meaning her father, her brother Hanzalah, her grandfather ʿUtbah, his brother Shaybah, and the other idolaters who were with them at Badr.

names.arabic: قريبة بنت أبي سفيان بن حرب
names.english: Quraybah bint Abī Sufyān Ibn Ḥarb

records.english: The sister of al-Ṣiddīq. Ibn Saʿd mentioned her and stated that Qays b. Saʿd b. ʿUbadah married her, but she bore him no children. She was the full sister of Umm Farwah.

records.english: The ʿAtwārī woman. She was mentioned previously in the biography of her daughter ʿUqaylah al-ʿAtwariyyah under the unpointed letter ʿayn.

records.arabic: الكندية ذكرها أبو نعيم وأخرج لها من طريق عبد الرحمن بن عمرو بن جبلة أحد المتروكين قال حدثتنا ميسرة بنت حبشي الطائية عن قتيلة بنت عبد الله عن قسرة الكندية قالت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيا قسرة اذكري الله عند الخطيئة يذكرك عند المغفرة وأطيعي زوجك يكفك شر الدنيا والآخرة وبري والديك يكثر خير بيتك قال أبو عمر بكسر القاف وسكون المهملة وقال غيره بالشين المعجمة وقيل بفتح القاف مع إهمال السين
records.english: The Kindī woman. Abu Nuʿaym mentioned her and transmitted for her through ʿAbd al-Rahman b. ʿAmr b. Jabalah, one of the abandoned transmitters, who said: Maysarah bt. Habashi al-Taʾiyyah related to us, from Qutaylah bt. ʿAbd Allah, from Qasarah al-Kindiyyah, who said: The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “O Qasarah, remember God when you sin, and He will remember you with forgiveness. Obey your husband, and he will spare you the evil of this world and the next. Be dutiful to your parents, and the good in your household will increase.” Abu ʿUmar said that the qaf has a kasrah and the unpointed letter is unvocalized. Another authority said it was with the dotted shin. It is also said to have an open qaf and an unpointed sin.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن عمرو بن جبلة
names.english: ʿAbd al-Rahman b. ʿAmr b. Jabalah

records.english: With qāf and then fāʾ, in the diminutive; the Hilālī woman. She was also called Mulaykah. Abu ʿAli al-Ghassani said in his supplement to al-Istiʿab: Muslim mentioned her among those from whom only one narrator transmitted. He said: She was the wife of ʿAbd Allah b. Abi Hadrad, and no one other than al-Aʿraj related from her.

records.english: Ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Qays. She was the wife of Sulayt b. ʿAmr. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that she and her husband emigrated to Abyssinia, then returned to Medina with the people of the two ships.

records.arabic: التميمية ثم من بني العنبر ومنهم من نسبها غنوية فصحف هاجرت إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع حريث بن حسان وافد بني بكر بن وائل روى حديثها عبد الله بن حسان العنبري عن جدتيه صفية ودحيبة ابنتي عليبة وكانت ربيبتي قيلة وكانت قيلة جدة أبيها أنها قالت قدمت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الحديث بطوله أخرجه الطبراني مطولا وأخرج البخاري في الأدب المفرد طرفا منه وأبو داود طرفا منه أيضا والترمذي من أول المرفوع إلى قوله يتعاونان قال فذكر الحديث بطوله وقال لا نعرفه إلا من حديث عبد الله بن حسان قال أبو عمر هو حديث طويل فصيح حسن وقد شرحه أهل العلم بالغريب وقال أبو علي بن السكن روى عنها حديث طويل فيه كلام فصيح وساقه من طريق عن عبد الله بن حسان مختصرا وقال لم يروه غير عبد الله بن حسان وقال فيه إن أم قيلة صفية بنت صيفي أخت أكثم بن صيفي قلت ساقه الطبراني وابن منده بطوله وهذا لفظ بن منده من طرق ثلاثة عن عبد الله بن حسان بهذا السند أنها أخبرتهما أنها كانت تحت حبيب بن أزهر أحد بن جناب فولدت النساء ثم توفي فانتزع بناتها منها ثوب بن أزهر وهو عمهن فخرجت تبتغي الصحبة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في أول الإسلام أي إسلام قومها فبكت جويرية منهن هي أصغرهن حديباء كانت قد أخذتها الفرصة عليها مسح من صوف فاحتملتها معها فبينما هما 343 ترتكان الجمل إذا انتفجت الأرنب فقالت الحديباء الفصية لا والله لا يزال كعبك أعلى من كعب أثوب في هذا الحديث أبدا ثم لم لما سنح الثعلب سمته اسما غير الثعلب فقالت فيه ما قالت في الأرنب فبينما هما ترتكان الجمل إذ بكر وأخذته رعدة فقالت الحديباء أدركتك والأمانة أخذة أثوب قال فقلت واضطررت إليها ويحك فما أصنع قالت قلبي ثيابك ظهورها لبطونها وتدحرجي ظهرك لبطنك وقلبي أحلاس جملك ثم جعلت سبيجها فقلبتها ثم تدحرجت ظهرها لبطنها ففعلت ما أمرتني به فانتقض الجمل فقام فناخ وبال فقالت أعيدي عليه أذانك ففعلت ثم خبا يرتد فإذا أثوب يسعى على آثارنا بالسيف صلتا فوألنا إلى حواء ضخم فداره حيث ألقى الجمل إلى رواق البيت الأوسط وكان جملا ذلولا ثم اقتحم داخله فأدركني أثوب بالسيف فأصابت ظبته طائفة من فرويته فقال ألقى إلي ابنة أخي يا دفار فرمت بها إليه فجعلها على منكبه فذهب بها فكنت أعلم به من أهل البيت فمضيت إلى أخت لي ناكح في بني شيبان أبتغي الصحابة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فبينا أنا عندها ذات ليلة من الليالي تحسب أني نائمة إذ جاء زوجها من السامر فقال وأبيك لقد وجدت لفيلة صاحب صدق فقالت أختي من هو فقال هو حريث بن حسان الشيباني وافد بكر بن وائل فقالت أختي الويل لي لا تخبر بهذا أختي فتذهب مع أخي بكر بن وائل بين سمع الأرض وبصرها ليس معها من قومها رجل قال لا ذكرته لها قالت وأنا غير ذاكرة لهذا فغدوت وشددت على جمل وسمعت قائلا يقول فنشدت عنه فوجدته غير بعيد وسألته الصحبة فقال نعم وكرامة وركابه مناخة عنده فخرجنا معه صاحب صدق حتى قدمنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي بالناس صلاة الغداة قد أقيمت حين شق الفجر والنجوم شابكة في السماء والرجال لا تكاد تعارف مع ظلمة الليل فصففت مع الرجال وأنا امرأة حديثه عهد بالجاهلية فقال لي الرجل الذي يليني من الصف امرأة أنت أم رجل فقلت لا بل امرأة فقال إنك كدت تفتنيني فصلى وراءك في النساء فإذا صف من النساء قد حدث عند الحجرات لم أكن رأيته حيث دخلت فكنت معهن فلما طلعت الشمس دنوت فكنت إذا رأيت رجلا ذا رواء وذا قشر طمح إليه بصري لأرى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فوق الناس فلما ارتفعت الشمس جاء رجل فقال السلام عليك يا رسول الله فقال وعليك السلام ورحمة الله وعليه أسمال مليتين قد كانت مزعفرتين وقد نقضتا وبيده عسيب نخلة قفر غير خوصتين من أعلاه وهو قاعد القرفصاء فلما رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المتخشع في الجلسة أرعدت من الفرق فقال لي جليسه يا رسول الله أرعدت المسكينة فقال بيده ولم ينظر إلي وأنا عند ظهره يا مسكينة عليك السكينة فلما قالها أذهب الله ما كان في قلبي من الرعب وتقدم صاحبي فبايعه على الإسلام وعلى قومه ثم قال يا رسول الله اكتب بيننا وبين بني تميم بالدهناء لا يجاوزها إلينا إلا مسافر أو مجاوز فقال اكتب له يا غلام بالدهناء فلما رأيته قد أمر له بها شخص بن وهي وطني وداري فقلت يا رسول الله إنه لم يسألك السوية من الأرض إذ سألك إنما هي الدهناء مقيد الجمل ومرعي الغنم ونساء بني تميم وأبناؤها وراء ذلك فقال أمسك يا غلام صدقت المسكينة المسلم أخو المسلم يسعهما الماء والشجر ويتعاونان على الفتان فلما رأى حريث أنه قد حيل دون كتابه ضرب بيديه إحداهما على الأخرى ثم قال كنت أنا وأنت كما قال حتفها ضائن تحمل بأظلافها فقلت أنا والله ما علمت إن كنت لدليلا في الظلماء جوادا أبدى الرجل عفيفا عن الرفيقة حتى قدمنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولكن لا تلمني أن أسأل حظي إذا سألت حظك فقال وما حظك في الدهناء لا أبا لك فقلت مقيد جملي تسأله لجمل امرأتك فقال لا جرم أني أشهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أني لك لا أزال أخا ما حييت إذا أثنيت على هذا عنده فقلت أما إذ بدأتها فلن أضيعها فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أيلام أهل ود أن يفصل الخطة أو ينتظر من وراء الحجزة قالت فبكيت فقلت والله يا رسول الله لقد كنت ولد حرام فقاتل معك يوم الربذة ثم ذهب يمتري من خيبر فأصابته حماها فمات فقال والذي نفسي بيده لو لم تكوني مسكينة لجررناك على وجهك أتغلب إحداهن أن تصاحب صويحبة في الدنيا معروفا فإذا حال بينه وبينه من هو أولى به استرجع ثم قال رب أنسني ما أمضيت وأعني على ما أبقيت فوالذي نفس محمد بيده إن إحدا كن لتبكي فتستعيذ إليه صويحبة فيا عباد الله لا تعذبوا إخوانكم ثم كتب لها في قطعة أديم أحمر لقيلة والنسوة بنات قيلة بأن لا يظلمن حقا ولا يكرهن على منكر وكل مؤمن مسلم لهن نصير حسن ولا يسأن
records.english: The Tamīmī woman, of Banū al-ʿAnbar. Some attributed her to Ghaniyy, which is a scribal error. She emigrated to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم with Hurayth b. Hassan, the envoy of Banu Bakr b. Waʾil. ʿAbd Allah b. Hassan al-ʿAnbari related her report from his two grandmothers, Safiyyah and Duhaybah, daughters of ʿUlaybah, who were Qaylah's stepdaughters; Qaylah was the grandmother of their father. They related that she said: “I came to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم,” followed by the lengthy report. Al-Tabarani transmitted it in full. Al-Bukhari transmitted a portion in al-Adab al-Mufrad, Abu Dawud another portion, and al-Tirmidhi from the beginning of the marfuʿ portion through the words, “They cooperate with one another.” He then said that the narrator cited the report in full and added, “We know it only through the hadith of ʿAbd Allah b. Hassan.” Abu ʿUmar said: It is a long, eloquent, fine report, and scholars of rare vocabulary have explained it. Abu ʿAli b. al-Sakan said: A lengthy report containing eloquent speech was related from her. He gave it in abridged form through a route from ʿAbd Allah b. Hassan and said: No one other than ʿAbd Allah b. Hassan related it. He said in it that Qaylah's mother was Safiyyah bt. Sayfi, sister of Aktham b. Sayfi. I say: Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mandah gave it in full. The following is Ibn Mandah's wording, through three routes from ʿAbd Allah b. Hassan with this chain: Qaylah informed the two women that she had been married to Hubayb b. Azhar, one of Banu Jinab, and had borne daughters. Then he died, and Thawb b. Azhar, their paternal uncle, took her daughters from her. She set out seeking someone to accompany her to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم at the beginning of Islam—that is, the Islam of her people. A little girl among them, the youngest, named Hudayba, wept. An opportunity had come to take her; she wore a woolen wrap, so Qaylah carried her along. As the two were making the camel move, [343] a hare sprang out. Hudayba, who was perceptive, said, “No, by God, your heel shall always remain higher than Thawb's heel in this affair.” Then a fox crossed their path; she called it by a name other than “fox” and said about it what she had said about the hare. As they were making the camel move, it bolted and began to tremble. Hudayba said, “Thawb's seizure has overtaken you, by the trust.” I said, compelled to rely on her, “Woe to you, what shall I do?” She said, “Turn your garments inside out, roll over from your back onto your belly, and turn your camel's saddlecloths over.” Then she turned her own small wrap inside out and rolled from her back onto her belly. I did as she instructed. The camel shook off the affliction, rose, knelt, and urinated. She said, “Repeat your call over it.” I did so, and it began to go back and forth. Then Thawb appeared, running upon our tracks with his sword drawn. We took refuge in a great enclosure, and I drove the camel around it until it threw itself down at the portico of the middle tent; it was a docile camel. Then Thawb burst inside and overtook me with the sword. The edge of its blade struck part of my fur wrap. He said, “Throw my brother's daughter to me, you foul woman!” I threw her to him; he put her on his shoulder and took her away. I was the most knowledgeable person in the household about him. I went to a sister of mine who was married among Banu Shayban, seeking someone to accompany me to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. One night, while I was with her and she thought me asleep, her husband returned from an evening gathering and said, “By your father, I have found a trustworthy companion for Qaylah.” My sister asked, “Who is he?” He replied, “Hurayth b. Hassan al-Shaybani, the envoy of Bakr b. Waʾil.” My sister said, “Woe is me! Do not tell my sister this, lest she go with the brother of Bakr b. Waʾil across the land as far as hearing and sight reach, with no man of her people accompanying her.” He said, “I shall not mention it to her.” She replied, “Nor shall I mention it.” I set out at dawn, tightened the saddle on a camel, and heard a caller speaking. I inquired about him, found him not far away, and asked him for companionship. He replied, “Yes, and gladly.” His mounts were kneeling beside him. We traveled with him, a trustworthy companion, until we reached the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم while he was leading the people in the dawn prayer. The prayer had begun when daybreak split, the stars were interlaced in the sky, and the men could scarcely recognize one another in the darkness of night. I stood in the line with the men, being a woman only recently removed from the pre-Islamic period. The man next to me in the line asked, “Are you a woman or a man?” I replied, “No, a woman.” He said, “You nearly tempted me. Pray behind you with the women.” A line of women had formed by the apartments, which I had not seen when I entered, so I joined them. When the sun rose, I drew near. Whenever I saw a man of handsome appearance and fine clothing, my gaze would rise toward him, seeking to identify the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم among the people. When the sun had risen, a man came and said, “السلام عليك يا رسول الله.” He replied, “وعليك السلام ورحمة الله.” He wore the worn remnants of two garments that had once been dyed with saffron but had faded. In his hand was the bare stalk of a palm frond, with only two leaflets remaining at its top, and he was sitting with his legs drawn up. When I saw the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم sitting so humbly, I began to tremble with fear. The man seated beside him said, “O Messenger of God, the poor woman is trembling.” Without looking at me, while I was behind him, he gestured with his hand and said, “Poor woman, be calm.” When he said this, God removed the fear that had been in my heart. My companion stepped forward and pledged himself and his people to Islam. He then said, “O Messenger of God, write an agreement between us and Banu Tamim concerning al-Dahnaʾ, so that no one of them may cross it toward us except a traveler or one passing through.” He said, “Boy, write for him concerning al-Dahnaʾ.” When I saw that he had ordered it granted to him, I rose, for it was my homeland and dwelling. I said, “O Messenger of God, he did not ask you for a fair portion of the land when he asked. Al-Dahnaʾ is where the camel is tethered and sheep graze, and behind it are the women and children of Banu Tamim.” He said, “Stop, boy. The poor woman has spoken truly. A Muslim is a Muslim's brother; water and trees suffice them both, and they cooperate against those who cause strife.” When Hurayth saw that his document had been prevented, he struck one hand against the other and said, “You and I have become like the saying: ‘A sheep carries its own death upon its hooves.’” I replied, “By God, so far as I knew, you were a guide through the darkness, generous and plainly a man, and chaste toward your female companion until we reached the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم. But do not blame me for asking for my share when you asked for yours.” He asked, “What share have you in al-Dahnaʾ, may you have no father?” I replied, “The tethering place of my camel—you ask it for your wife's camel!” He said, “Assuredly, I call the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم to witness that I shall remain your brother as long as I live, since you praised me in his presence.” I said, “Since you began it, I shall not let it go to waste.” The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Are the family of a beloved person blamed if they separate the claim, or wait behind the barrier?” She said: I wept and said, “By God, O Messenger of God, I had a son named Haram who fought alongside you on the day of al-Rabadhah. Then he went to purchase provisions from Khaybar, its fever struck him, and he died.” He said, “By the One in whose hand is my soul, were you not a poor woman, we would have dragged you on your face! Is one of you unable to keep honorable company with her little companion in this world, then, when one with a greater claim than she comes between them, to say, ‘We belong to God and to Him we return’? Then say: ‘Lord, console me for what You have taken and help me concerning what You have left.’ By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, one of you women will weep while her little companion seeks refuge with him. O servants of God, do not torment your brothers.” He then wrote for her, on a piece of red leather, an instrument for Qaylah and the women, the daughters of Qaylah: that they should not be deprived of any right, should not be compelled to do wrong, and that every Muslim believer should be a good supporter for them; the text then ends with a damaged clause whose subject and object are unclear.

records.arabic: يقال لها أم بني أنمار وأخت بني أنمار وقال الطبري العقيلية وقال بن أبي خيثمة الأنصارية أخت بني أنمار لها صحبة وأخرج حديثها هو وابن ماجة من طريق عبد الله بن عثمان بن خثيم عنها قالت رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عند المروة يحل من عمرة له فقلت أني امرأة أشتري وأبيع فأستام أكثر مما أريد ثم أنقص الحديث وفيه لا تفعلي وأخرجه بن سعد من طريق بن خثيم مطولا وأخرجه بن السكن ووقع في روايته أن عبد الله بن عثمان بن خثيم قال إنه سمع قيلة وقال الفاكهي دار أم أنمار بمكة وكانت برزة من النساء بأخرة
records.english: She is called the mother of Banū Anmār and the sister of Banū Anmār. Al-Tabari called her al-ʿUqayliyyah, while Ibn Abi Khaythamah called her an Ansari woman, sister of Bani Anmar. She had companionship. He and Ibn Majah transmitted her report through ʿAbd Allah b. ʿUthman b. Khuthaym, from her. She said: I saw the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم at al-Marwah, releasing himself from the consecrated state of one of his lesser pilgrimages. I said, “I am a woman who buys and sells. I ask more than I actually intend to pay, then reduce,” to the end of the report. It includes, “Do not do that.” Ibn Saʿd transmitted it at length through Ibn Khuthaym, and Ibn al-Sakan also transmitted it. In his recension, ʿAbd Allah b. ʿUthman b. Khuthaym said that he heard Qaylah. Al-Fakihi said: Umm Anmar had a house in Mecca, and in later life she was a woman who appeared openly in public.

records.english: The mother of Sibāʿ ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAmr ibn Naḍlah. She was among the allies of Banu Zuhrah. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr mentioned her and said that her case requires examination.

records.arabic: بن معد يكرب الكندية أخت الأشعث بن قيس قاله أبو عمر ويقال قيلة تزوجها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سنة عشر ومات ولم تك قدمت عليه ولا رآها ولا دخل بها وقيل كان تزويجه إياها قبل وفاته بشهرين وقيل تزوجها في مرض موته وقيل أوصى أن تخبر فإن شاءت ضربه عليها الحجاب وتحرم على المؤمنين وإن شاءت فلتنكح من شاءت فاختارت النكاح فتزوجتها عكرمة بحضرموت فبلغ أبا بكر فقال لقد هممت أن أحرق عليهما بيتهما فقال له عمر ما هي من أمهات المؤمنين ولا دخل بها ولا ضرب عليها الحجاب وقال بعضهم مات قبل خروجها من اليمن فحلف عليها عكرمة وقيل أنها ارتدت فاحتج عمر على أبي بكر بأنها ليست من أزواج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بارتدادها فقال ولم تلد لعكرمة والاختلاف فيها كثير جدا انتهى كلام بن عبد البر وأخرج 244 أبو نعيم من طريق إسحاق بن حبيب الشهيدي عن عبد الأعلى عن داود بن أبي هند عن عكرمة عن بن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تزوج قيلة أخت الأشعث ومات قبل أن يخبرها وهذا موصول قوي الإسناد أيضا وأخرجه أيضا من طريق عبد الوهاب الثقفي عن داود عن الشعبي مرسلا ولفظه قتيلة بنت الأشعث ومات فتزوجها عكرمة فشق على أبي بكر فذكر كلام عمر المتقدم وفي آخره فاطمأن أبو بكر وسكن
records.english: Ibn Maʿdīkarib, the Kindī woman. She was the sister of al-Ashʿath b. Qays. Abu ʿUmar stated this. It is said that the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم married Qaylah in the year ten, but died before she had come to him; he had neither seen her nor consummated the marriage. It is said that he married her two months before his death, and also that he married her during his final illness. It is also said that he instructed that she be given a choice: if she wished, the veil would be imposed upon her and she would be forbidden to the believers; if she wished, she could marry whomever she chose. She chose marriage, and ʿIkrimah married her in Hadramawt. When Abu Bakr learned of it, he said, “I nearly burned their house down over them.” ʿUmar said to him, “She is not one of the Mothers of the Believers. He did not consummate the marriage with her and did not impose the veil upon her.” Some said that he died before she departed Yemen, and ʿIkrimah married her. It is also said that she apostatized, so ʿUmar argued to Abu Bakr that by apostatizing she was not one of the wives of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. She bore no child to ʿIkrimah. The disagreement concerning her is extremely extensive. Here ends Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr's discussion. Abu Nuʿaym [244] transmitted through Ishaq b. Habib al-Shahidi, from ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Dawud b. Abi Hind, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم married Qaylah, sister of al-Ashʿath, and died before she was informed. This is connected and also has a strong chain. He also transmitted through ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi, from Dawud, from al-Shaʿbi, in mursal form, with the wording: “Qutaylah bt. al-Ashʿath.” He died, then ʿIkrimah married her, which distressed Abu Bakr. He then cited ʿUmar's foregoing words. At the end it says: Abu Bakr was reassured and calmed down.

names.arabic: قيلة بنت قيس بن معد يكرب

records.arabic: العتوارية أخرج حديثها بن منده من طريق حفص بن عمر عن بكار بن عبد العزيز عن موسى بن عبيدة حدثنا يزيد بن عبد الرحمن عن أمه حجة بنت قرط عن أمها عقيلة بنت عبيد بن الحارث قال جئت أنا وأمي قريبة بنت الحارث العتوارية كذا عنده والصواب قريرة براء بدل الموحدة كما تقدم في عقيلة في حرف العين قال أبو نعيم ترجم بن منده قريبة وساق الحديث فقال في روايته قريرة وكذا ساقه الطبراني وغيره قلت هو الصواب
records.english: The ʿAtwārī woman. Ibn Mandah transmitted her report through Hafs b. ʿUmar, from Bakkar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from Musa b. ʿUbaydah: Yazid b. ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, from his mother Hajjah bt. Qurt, from her mother ʿUqaylah bt. ʿUbayd b. al-Harith, who said, “My mother Quraybah bt. al-Harith al-ʿAtwariyyah and I came...” Thus it appears in his work. The correct form is Qurayrah, with ra instead of ba, as was given previously under ʿUqaylah under the letter ʿayn. Abu Nuʿaym said: Ibn Mandah gave the heading Quraybah, but in the report itself his recension reads Qurayrah. Al-Tabarani and others likewise transmitted it. I say: That is the correct form.

records.arabic: أسعد بن زرارة تقدم نسبها في ترجمة أبيها وأوصى بها أبوها إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فتزوجها عبد الله بن أبي حبيبة من بني الأغر بن زيد بن العطاف وكانت أصغر بنات أسعد وكانت من المبايعات وقد تقدم ذكرها في ترجمة أختها حبيبة
records.english: Asʿad ibn Zurārah. Her lineage was given previously in her father's biography. Her father entrusted her to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. ʿAbd Allah b. Abi Habibah of Banu al-Agharr b. Zayd b. al-ʿAttaf married her. She was the youngest of Asʿad's daughters and was among the women who gave the pledge. She was mentioned previously in the biography of her sister Habibah.

records.english: Ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAtīk ibn ʿAmr ibn Mabdhūl. Her kunya was Umm Saʿid. Ibn Saʿd mentioned her among the women who gave the pledge. He said: Her mother was Muʿadhah bt. Anas b. Qays b. ʿUbayd. Yazid b. Abi al-Yusr Kaʿb b. ʿAmr married her, and she bore him Saʿid, ʿAbd al-Rahman, and Umm Kathir.

records.arabic: بن حرام أخت حسان لأبيه من بني مالك بن النجار وأخرج حديثها الترمذي وأبو يعلى من طريق يزيد بن يزيد بن جابر عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة عن جدته كبشة قالت دخل علي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فشرب من في قربة قائما معلقة فقمت إلى فمها فقطعته كذا في خبرها فيه ذكر أبيها ولا نسب ونسبها أبو عروبة كما ذكرت ورواه عبد العزيز بن الحصين عن يزيد عن عبد الرحمن فقال عن جدته البرصاء أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم شرب وهو قائم أخرجه بن منده وكأنه لقيها ورواه بن وهب عن بن لهيعة عن يزيد فقال عن جدته كلثم وستأتي وقال بن سعد أمها سخطى بنت حارثة بن لوذان تزوجها عمرو بن محصن بن عمرو بن عتيك فولدت له ثعلبة وأبا عمرو وأبا حبيبة ثم تزوجها الحارث بن ثعلبة فولدت له أم ثابت رملة ثم تزوجها حارثة بن النعمان
records.english: Ibn Ḥarām. She was Hassan's paternal half-sister, of Banu Malik b. al-Najjar. Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Yaʿla transmitted her report through Yazid b. Yazid b. Jabir, from ʿAbd al-Rahman b. Abi ʿAmrah, from his grandmother Kabshah, who said: “The Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم entered upon me and drank while standing from the mouth of a hanging waterskin. I rose and cut off its mouth.” Thus her report mentions her father but does not give her lineage. Abu ʿArubah gave her lineage as I have stated it. ʿAbd al-ʿAziz b. al-Husayn related it from Yazid, from ʿAbd al-Rahman, but said: from his grandmother al-Barsaʾ, that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم drank while standing. Ibn Mandah transmitted it, and it appears that he met her. Ibn Wahb related it from Ibn Lahiʿah, from Yazid, but said: from his grandmother Kulthum, who will appear later. Ibn Saʿd said: Her mother was Sakhta bt. Harithah b. Lawdhan. ʿAmr b. Mihsan b. ʿAmr b. ʿAtik married her, and she bore him Thaʿlabah, Abu ʿAmr, and Abu Habibah. Then al-Harith b. Thaʿlabah married her, and she bore him Umm Thabit Ramlah. Then Harithah b. al-Nuʿman married her.

بن عبيد بن ثعلبة بن الأبجر وهو خدرة الأنصارية الخدرية والدة سعد بن معاذ عاشت حتى مات وندبته بقولها
ويل أم سعد سعدا
صرامة وجدا ذكر ذلك بن إسحاق في قصة موت سعد قال فذكروا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال كل نادبة تكذب إلا نادبة سعد
records.english: Ibn ʿUbayd ibn Thaʿlabah ibn al-Abjar, who was Khudrah, the Anṣārī Khudrī woman. She was the mother of Saʿd b. Muʿadh. She lived until he died and lamented him with her words: “Woe to Saʿd's mother for Saʿd, / for resolve and intense feeling.” Ibn Ishaq mentioned this in the story of Saʿd's death. He said: They related that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Every woman who laments speaks falsely except the woman who laments Saʿd.”

records.arabic: بن مالك الأنصارية زوج عبد الله بن أبي قتادة قال بن حبان لها صحبة وتبعه المستغفري وحديثها عن أبي قتادة في سؤر الهر في الموطأ والسنن الأربعة وقال بن سعد تزوجها ثابت بن أبي قتادة فولدت له أمها صفية من أهل اليمن
records.english: Ibn Mālik, the Anṣārī woman. She was the wife of ʿAbd Allah b. Abi Qatadah. Ibn Hibban said that she had companionship, and al-Mustaghfiri followed him. Her report from Abu Qatadah concerning water left by a cat appears in al-Muwattaʾ and the four Sunan collections. Ibn Saʿd said: Thabit b. Abi Qatadah married her, and she bore him. Her mother was Safiyyah, one of the people of Yemen.

records.arabic: عمة الأشعث بن قيس وهي والدة معاوية بن حديج الصحابي المعروف روى قصتها الدارقطني من طريق ولدها معاوية أنه قال قدمت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعي أمي كبشة بنت معد يكرب عمة الأشعث فقالت يا رسول الله أني آليت أن أطوف بالبيت حبوا فقال طوفي على رجليك سبعين سبعا عن يديك وسبعا عن رجليك وسنده ضعيف استدركها بن الدباغ وغيره على الاستيعاب
records.english: The paternal aunt of al-Ashʿath ibn Qays. She was the mother of Muʿawiyah b. Hudayj, the well-known Companion. Al-Daraqutni related her story through her son Muʿawiyah, who said: I came to the Messenger of God صلى الله عليه وسلم accompanied by my mother Kabshah bt. Maʿdi Karib, the paternal aunt of al-Ashʿath. She said, “O Messenger of God, I vowed that I would circumambulate the House crawling.” He replied, “Circumambulate on your feet seventy circuits: seven on behalf of your hands and seven on behalf of your feet.” Its chain is weak. Ibn al-Dabbagh and others included her as an addendum to al-Istiʿab.

records.arabic: بن عاصم الأنصارية كانت زوج أبي قيس بن الأسلت ويقال لها كبيشة قال بن جريج عن عكرمة نزلت فيها فيها لا يحل لكم أن ترثوا النساء كرها أخرجه أبو موسى عن المستغفري ثم من طريق أبي ثور عن بن جريج وذكرته في الأنساب من عدة طرق
records.english: Ibn ʿĀṣim, the Anṣārī woman. She was the wife of Abu Qays b. al-Aslat and was also called Kubayshah. Ibn Jurayj related from ʿIkrimah that concerning her the verse was revealed, “It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will.” Abu Musa transmitted it from al-Mustaghfiri, then through Abu Thawr, from Ibn Jurayj. I have mentioned it in al-Ansab through several routes.

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن عامر بن زيد مناة وعمرو هو بن الإطنابة من بني الحارث بن الخزرج ذكرها بن حبيب في المبايعات وهي أم عبد الله بن رواحة وكذا ذكرها بن سعد ويقال فيها كبيشة بالتصغير وزاد ولما مات رواحة خلف عليها قيس بن شماس فولدت له ثابتا
records.english: Ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir ibn Zayd Manāt. ʿAmr is Ibn al-Itnabah—of Banu al-Harith b. al-Khazraj. Ibn Habib mentioned her among the women who gave the pledge. She was the mother of ʿAbd Allah b. Rawahah; Ibn Saʿd likewise mentioned her. She is also called Kubayshah, in the diminutive. He added: When Rawahah died, Qays b. Shammas married her, and she bore him Thabit.

names.arabic: كبشة بنت واقد بن عمرو بن عامر بن زيد مناة
names.english: Kabshah bint Wāqid Ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿĀmir ibn Zayd Manāt
